data.narrative:
Standard Nuclear, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Kurt Terrani, has raised $182M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 11 firms—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Valar Atomics, Helion, Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo—all operating in the same sector and stage band.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $470M total-raised proxy as a base and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding $940M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Valar Atomics at $6.0B Series B, Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M Seed, Fuse Energy at $200M Series A) produces a median of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity and varying technology maturity within the nuclear energy sector.

The triangulated valuation range is $687M (low), $874M (median), and $1.1B (high). This $400M band reflects meaningful uncertainty around stage-appropriate pricing and peer selection. Key sensitivities include the peer median's heavy dependence on a small sample spanning multiple stages, and the stage-progression method's reliance on historical multipliers in a nascent, heterogeneous sector. Tighter conviction would require additional same-stage, same-technology-type comparables.
